sc: Child with cough, fast breathing and chest indrawing, drinking well → Pneumonia: oral amoxicillin 5 days
Cough with inability to drink, convulsions or SpO2 < 90% → Severe pneumonia: admit, ampicillin + gentamicin
School child, dry cough for a week, X-ray worse than the child → Mycoplasma: azithromycin
f: Fast breathing (best sign) · chest indrawing · crackles, bronchial breathing · dull percussion · hypoxia
S. pneumoniae (commonest bacterial) · viruses/RSV (infants) · Staph (boils, measles, pneumatoceles) · Mycoplasma (school age) · PCP (HIV)
Pulse oximetry (decides oxygen) · chest X-ray if severe or not improving · blood culture · ultrasound for effusion
Amoxicillin 40 mg/kg twice daily · severe: ampicillin 50 mg/kg 6-hourly + gentamicin 7.5 mg/kg daily · oxygen if SpO2 < 90%
Empyema (stony dull, pH < 7.2 → drain) · lung abscess · pneumothorax · sepsis · no improvement in 48 h → reassess
trap: The best sign of pneumonia is fast breathing, not crackles · recurrent pneumonia in the same lobe → foreign body · different lobes + poor growth → CF · trachea pushed away = effusion, pulled = collapse
